newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank says no repo tender on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank says no repo tender on Wednesday.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said it would not hold a repo tender on Wednesday.

"We decided not to hold the repo operation today since, according to our monitoring of the market situtation, the interbank liquidity appears sufficient," said Peter Andresic, head of the NBS Open Market Operation Department.

Andresic said Tuesday's volume of commercial banks' minimum reserves, deposited in the NBS, slightly exceeded the required amount and that the central bank expected banks further to improve fulfilment of their minimum reserves requirement in coming days.
The NBS added 2.0 billion crowns into the interbank market through a three-day repo tender on Tuesday, with average yield falling to 16.74 percent from 18.82 percent on Monday.
The central bank monitors market liquidity on a daily basis and decides each morning whether to hold any open market operations.
According to NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector as of July 22 lacked 2.70 percent of the cumulative funds needed to meet minimum reserves requirements on July 31.
